PullRequest.Title: Enhance structural diff provider for top-level code and test handling
PullRequest.Body: Improve support for categorizing top-level code in structural diffs and enhance the EntityInfo interface for better code structure representation. Streamline test and suite registrations to allow for nested test structures, and introduce utility functions for managing test titles and spans.

Scenarios.Scenario: Expand working-tree or staged TypeScript structural changes using TS6, including top-level registrations, imports/exports, and documentation edits.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Resolve the two text models, compute a complete textual diff, invoke the extension provider, parse and classify both supplied texts in tsserver, convert and validate the pruned result, then populate structural children. Structural analysis is requested on expansion rather than application startup.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve original and modified text model references, potentially reading working-file or Git snapshot content.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two model resolutions per uncached resource, started together; existing loaded models can avoid physical reads.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same two model references were resolved before the PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Both resolutions finish before structural computation begins.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Compute the textual diff in the editor worker and dispatch the chosen structural provider to the extension host.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One worker computation and one dispatch to the selected successful provider per uncached pair; fallback provider selection remains sequential.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The worker and extension-host dispatch path and call counts are unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Textual diff and provider completion precede publication of structural children.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send both complete texts and change offsets through typescript.tsserverRequest; receive the structural tree.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request normally, at most two when the existing handler-initialization retry runs; no requests per declaration, registration, or test.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same complete-text request and retry existed. The diff changes entity representation, not request frequency.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited before result conversion and publication.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Open the backing document after an initial request failure so tsserver can initialize its project and plugin.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one open per failed initial request; not performed on normal successful requests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical failure-only open and retry behavior.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize the pruned protocol result and convert its changed entities and coverage ranges.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One result per pair; size follows changed output entities and their ancestors, rather than all collected AST nodes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Results were already pruned and converted once. New top-level and test items alter meaningful output content, without establishing redundant serialization or unbounded retention.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Conversion completes before structural children are available.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One original/modified pair per expanded SCM resource; source bytes, structural declarations and registrations, and textual change count determine local analysis cost. Top-level statements are grouped per file or namespace, not issued as separate server requests.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: SCM limits active loads to three. Provider selection is sequential, and TS6 computation is synchronous in the shared semantic tsserver with the existing low-priority request configuration. No per-statement parallelism was introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: SCM caches completed children and shares entry.pending; edits and lifecycle invalidation release the entry. TS6 reparses supplied texts on each uncached request, as before. Failure results remain cached until invalidation. A missing plugin handler can trigger one backing-document open and one retry.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the traced request path, bounded boundary cardinality, cache ownership, and synchronous analysis location. No high-confidence actionable regression mechanism established.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No timings or allocation profiles were available. Extremely deep compound statements or long fluent call chains were considered, but a realistic new high-cost scenario was not established independently of existing traversal costs.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. New representations and offset-based sibling matching do not create per-item I/O or IPC; collections are request-local and output remains pruned.

Scenarios.Scenario: Expand structural changes using TS7 native snapshots, including simultaneous staged and unstaged versions of a backing file.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After model resolution and textual diff, obtain the shared native API, open a snapshot, read original then modified supplied content through temporary updates, run synchronous structural computation in the extension host, dispose snapshots and close the file, then return the result.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve the two source text models.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two resolutions per uncached pair, potentially satisfied by existing loaded models.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Both precede textual and structural analysis.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Compute text changes through the worker and request structural interpretation in the extension host.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One text diff and one selected-provider dispatch per uncached pair.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited before native source acquisition and structural publication.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Activate the supported TypeScript extension, initialize an API connection, and connect to its language-server pipe.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One coalesced connection attempt normally on cold initialization, with the existing maximum of three attempts across restart races; warm requests reuse the connection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Shared connection, initialization coalescing, restart handling, and retry bound are unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold initialization precedes snapshots; warm requests avoid connection setup.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Open and close native snapshots, apply two temporary content updates, obtain default projects and source files, and dispose snapshots.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two explicit createSnapshot calls, two temporary-update workflows, at most two project lookups and two source-file reads per pair; two explicit snapshot disposals plus temporary snapshots owned by the SDK workflow. Counts do not scale with structural item count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The complete snapshot acquisition, sequential reads, and finally-block cleanup are unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Original and modified reads are sequential and precede computation; cleanup is awaited before return.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Return and convert the pruned structural tree to the main thread.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One result per pair, proportional to changed entities and necessary ancestors.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same conversion and result transfer existed; only meaningful entity content changes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must complete before SCM children are populated.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One snapshot workflow per uncached resource/version pair. Two source versions are analyzed regardless of the number of declarations, top-level calls, or tests.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: At most three active SCM loads; source versions within a request are read sequentially. Requests for independent resources or staged/unstaged pairs can overlap on the shared connection. No limiter, sequencing, or cache-clearing behavior changed.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: TypeScript7Connection coalesces in-flight API initialization and reuses a live connection; reconnect invalidates it. The provider clears its source-file cache once per analysis, as before. SCM result caching avoids reanalysis until invalidation; there is no new retained AST cache.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that the changed structural collector is reached after the unchanged snapshot workflow and that cleanup/cache ownership and external call cardinality remain unchanged.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The external native SDK implementation and measured AST/comment-access costs were not available. Repository call sites and tests establish constant per-pair semantic operations, not a new per-item native boundary.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable boundary fan-out, concurrency, cache-lifecycle, or cleanup regression. The diff does not modify provider snapshot scheduling or ownership.

Scenarios.Scenario: Classify suite/test registrations, nested test structures, and edits inside functions or methods.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Collect entities for both versions, recognize suites and tests, match siblings, classify text coverage, and prune unchanged nodes before returning through the selected TS6/TS7 workflow.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Return changed test/suite entities and their coverage through the already-existing provider result path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One result for the entire file pair. Only changed entities and ancestor suites survive pruning.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One pruned result was returned before; tests now have explicit title-based items while function-local declarations and helper items are no longer exhaustively listed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The entire pruned result precedes structural-tree publication.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Suite/test statements and declared members determine collected structural entities; callback AST size additionally affects test-span traversal in non-test files. Compound suite statements expose their syntactic tests, not runtime loop iterations. Offset matching adds a binary search over changes per modified sibling.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Both collectors and matching/classification run synchronously within their existing process. No asynchronous work or boundary request is issued per test; SCM's three-load bound still applies.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Entity maps, statement groups, test spans, and matching maps are local to one computation and become unreachable afterward. Test files skip the separate test-span scan; non-test files retain a traversal for tagging callbacks inside functions. Completed SCM results are cached under the existing lifecycle.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in request-local lifetime, syntactic cardinality, pruning, binary-search matching, and absence of per-test external operations.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No measured costs for large suite trees were supplied. New call-body arrays, title normalization, compound-span subtraction, and fluent-chain recognition were inspected; no realistic, high-confidence actionable regression was established against the previous exhaustive AST traversal.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The semantic restructuring is not by itself evidence of excessive allocation or eager work; it also removes function-local entity construction. No concrete prior performance regression fix with sufficiently strong symptom evidence was identified for blame reporting.

Scenarios.Scenario: Restore many expanded SCM files or edit an already-expanded file repeatedly.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: An uncached resource waits for a load slot, model resolution, text diff, and provider completion. Cached structural children return immediately. Content changes invalidate the entry and schedule a view refresh before the next request.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Load two text models for each uncached expanded resource.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two model resolutions per distinct uncached resource, with at most three resource loads active; cached entries avoid them.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same per-resource coalescing, cache, limiter, and two-model loading existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Resource loading waits for its limiter slot and model completion.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Execute the selected TS6 request or TS7 snapshot workflow for each uncached pair.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One provider workflow per distinct uncached resource; TS6 retries only its initial failure and TS7 shares connection initialization. No calls for cached structural children.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same provider multiplicity and scheduling. Changed collectors do not alter SCM invalidation, debounce, pending sharing, or limiter behavior.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Provider completion gates each expanded resource's children.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Distinct expanded SCM resources after per-entry pending-request sharing, not individual structural children. Original/modified versions within one resource share one provider workflow.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: A shared Limiter permits three active loads, with a 30-second existing load budget. Provider calls within a load are sequential; synchronous TS6/TS7 classification remains serialized by the process event loop. No new per-child task scheduling or global concurrency burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: entry.pending coalesces concurrent requests for the same SCM resource; children caches success, empty results, and failure/status rows. Content changes, collapse/release, group removal, provider invalidation, and disposal release existing entries and references. Those mechanisms are unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the three-load limiter, per-resource coalescing, cached negative results, and lifecycle disposal.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Workspace resource counts and analysis durations vary; no profiling was performed. The effective resource concurrency and cache behavior are directly established in unchanged caller code.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable missing-coalescing, concurrency-burst, or retained-resource regression introduced by this PR.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass against base 4bb450d0b993177c934a60453067c88f9547e926. Inspected all six changed files and all diff pages, both structural-diff implementations, provider/caller paths, shared document handling, and relevant tests. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance finding or sufficiently evidenced regression-fix learning signal. Static review only; native SDK internals and measured performance were unavailable.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
